content.title: About
content.content: Soy milk is a plant‑based beverage made from soybeans. Unsweetened soy milk contains no added sugar, has a neutral flavor, and is often used as a dairy‑free alternative in vegan diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Commercial production of soy milk began in Japan in the early 20th century.
Soybeans are rich in protein, making soy milk one of the best plant‑based protein sources.
Unsweetened soy milk typically contains about 3 g of protein and 2 g of fat per 100 ml.
Many brands fortify soy milk with calcium, vitamin D, and vitamin B12 to match the nutritional profile of cow's milk.
In several countries soy is a declared allergen, so packaging must clearly state its presence.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A cup of unsweetened soy milk provides roughly 7 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Soy milk contains mainly polyunsaturated fatty acids, which are heart‑healthy.

items.title: Source of isoflavones
items.content: Soy isoflavones have antioxidant properties and may help balance hormones.

items.title: Fortified with calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Most products are enriched with calcium and vitamin D, aiding bone health.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Absence of lactose makes soy milk a safe choice for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy proteins, ranging from skin rashes to respiratory issues.

items.title: Phytoestrogens
items.content: High intake of isoflavones can affect hormonal balance; those with hormone‑sensitive conditions should consult a healthcare professional.

items.title: Additives and sweeteners
items.content: Certain brands add flavorings, stabilizers, or artificial sweeteners, which may be undesirable for sensitive consumers.

items.title: Genetically modified organisms (GMOs)
items.content: Most soybeans are GMO; choose non‑GMO labeled products if this is a concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soy milk can be drunk plain, added to smoothies, oatmeal, coffee, sauces, and baked goods. It is also commonly used in vegan sauces and creams.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cartons in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑taste.
